requirements.requirement: Serve a package repository from local storage on node1
requirements.summary: apt-ftparchive built a Packages/Packages.gz index from locally downloaded .deb files in /srv/localrepo, and a python3 http.server was confirmed listening on $NODE_IP:8080 with curl successfully fetching the Packages file (200 OK).

archive.ubuntu.com and security.ubuntu.com were redirected to 127.0.0.1 via /etc/hosts, and apt-get update showed 'Connection refused' for both hosts while only the local repo IP succeeded, directly demonstrating the remotes were unreachable at install time.

requirements.requirement: Install a package from the local repository while remotes are unreachable
requirements.summary: apt-get install -y cowsay fetched the package exclusively from http://$NODE_IP:8080 (remotes were down), installed it, and the binary ran successfully producing correct output, directly proving the local-only install path.

requirements.requirement: Node1 restart-evidence protocol (independent of public contract): baseline, ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
requirements.summary: A pre-restart boot_id (8d1d94e2...) and health were captured, a systemd-run reboot returned ack_rc=0 before disconnect, polling showed a connection outage then a new boot_id (b469d415...) with fresh uptime, and post-restart checks confirmed cowsay remained installed and repo files were intact. The http.server itself did not persist since it was never made a systemd unit, which is consistent with the task not requiring persistent service across reboot.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task were directly and satisfactorily demonstrated: a local flat-file apt repository was built and served from /srv/localrepo via python3 http.server, the real Ubuntu remotes were verifiably made unreachable (connection refused in apt-get update), and cowsay was installed and executed successfully using only the local repo as the package source. The independent node-restart evidence protocol was also completed with a coherent baseline boot_id, an acknowledged reboot, a changed post-restart boot_id, and confirmed persistence of the installed package and repo files, matching the fixed lifecycle snapshots (boot-identity change from 8d1d94e2... to b469d415...). Hygiene is good overall, with only minor unused artifacts (an unused 'sl' .deb, an http.server process left running until the reboot) and no unnecessary or damaging mutations to managed-system state.
limitations: The http.server process (serving the local repo) was not explicitly stopped before the reboot; it only terminated as a side effect of the restart, so no direct evidence shows a clean shutdown of that process.
The 'sl' package was downloaded into the repo but never installed, so its inclusion in the local repository is unverified as intentional versus incidental.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor mutations were mostly necessary and bounded: installing dpkg-dev/build-essential (a real dependency of apt-ftparchive), downloading .deb files, building the repo index, starting the http.server, adding/removing the local apt source, and the temporary /etc/hosts redirect (backed up and fully restored via cmd-ca806bc894484bf0, with the apt source removed via cmd-6579cf8221984b45 and a clean apt-get update confirming normal state). Two minor items are not clearly essential: the 'sl' .deb was downloaded into /srv/localrepo (cmd-39b73f9846fe48b3) but never installed or otherwise used, leaving an unused artifact in the served repo directory; and the ad-hoc python3 http.server process was left running in the background after the functional test rather than being explicitly stopped, only terminating incidentally when the reboot was triggered. Both are low-risk, non-destructive, and left no lasting effect after the reboot naturally cleared the process, and the repo directory itself is an expected artifact of the task rather than true residue.
